# Session import format

`DayActivity` → toolbar → **Import Session** lets you pick a `.json` file and merges it
into whichever day is currently open, without touching any previously logged history
(it only ever *adds* sets — see `DataStorage.mergeImportedSession()`).

This is the integration point for an external workout-generator script: have it write a
file in this format, and either open it with Verifit ("Open with...") or import it from
inside the app.

## Shape

```json
{
  "date": "2026-09-04",
  "comment": "Auto-generated by workout_engine.py",
  "exercises": [
    {
      "name": "Flat Barbell Bench Press",
      "bodyPart": "Chest",
      "comment": "Pause 90s between sets",
      "sets": [
        { "weight": 60, "reps": 8 },
        { "weight": 60, "reps": 8, "comment": "RPE 8" },
        { "weight": 60, "reps": 6 }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Squat",
      "sets": [
        { "weight": 100, "reps": 5 },
        { "weight": 100, "reps": 5 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Fields

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | no | `yyyy-MM-dd`. If omitted, the sets are added to whichever day you opened "Import Session" from. |
| `comment` | no | Day-level note. Currently read but not stored anywhere (the app has no concept of a day-level comment) — kept for forward compatibility. |
| `exercises[].name` | **yes** | Matched against known exercises by exact string (Verifit has no exercise IDs, only names — same reason "Duplicate Exercise" exists). A name not seen before is created automatically. |
| `exercises[].bodyPart` | no | One of `Chest`, `Back`, `Shoulders`, `Biceps`, `Triceps`, `Legs`, `Abs` (see `R.array.Categories`), but not enforced. Only used when `name` is a **new** exercise — if the exercise already exists, its existing body part is kept (a re-import never silently reclassifies it). Leave empty for a new exercise and just edit its category once in the app afterwards. |
| `exercises[].comment` | no | Per-exercise comment (e.g. machine settings), stored once per exercise for that day, same as the existing "add exercise" screen. |
| `exercises[].sets[].weight` | **yes** | kg, numeric. |
| `exercises[].sets[].reps` | **yes** | numeric. |
| `exercises[].sets[].comment` | no | Per-set comment. |

An exercise entry with no valid sets, or a set missing `weight`/`reps`, is skipped rather
than failing the whole import — the app reports how many sets were imported/skipped in a
toast.

## Design notes / constraints inherited from the app

- **No stable IDs.** Everything in Verifit (`Exercise`, and set→exercise linkage) is
  matched by exercise **name** as a plain string (`DataStorage.doesExerciseExist`,
  `editExercise`, `deleteExercise`, ...). There is nothing to key an import against
  except that name, so keep names byte-for-byte identical between your generator and the
  app if you want it to land on an existing exercise instead of creating a new one.
- **Additive, not a sync.** This intentionally does *not* reuse the existing CSV
  import/export path (`DataStorage.readFile`/`writeFile`, wired to Settings → "Import
  CSV") — that one is a full backup **restore** and clears all local data first. Session
  import only appends, so it's safe to run repeatedly / semi-automatically.
- **Re-importing the same file is not idempotent.** Running the same import twice will
  add the same sets twice (there's no de-duplication — the underlying `WorkoutSet` model
  has no external/import ID to dedupe on). If your script re-runs automatically, make
  sure it's the one deciding whether a session was already sent, or extend the format
  with an idempotency key later.
